cards.body:
## Summary
Move the pen conversation out of the Android module into core as a sans-IO state machine. The conversation covers pairing, the hello timeout, newest-pen-wins, ping, dispatch, and the heartbeat's choice of what to send each tick. The new pieces are `PairingDesk` (PIN, video aspect, generation counter), `PenConversation` (`onText(text)` and `onTick(nowMs)` return effects: `Send`, `Close`, `Deliver`, `Paired`) and `Heartbeat` (`beat(input)` returns an optional doc mirror, an optional thumbnail request and the state message). `PenSessionHost` shrinks to a coroutine driver: text and ticks go in, effects are carried out, and logging and the Thumbnailer stay on the Android side.

## Description
PenSessionHost.kt holds eleven behaviours: hello timeout, non-hello ignored, wrong-PIN reject, generation bump with welcome, stale-pen stand-down, ping on the receive path, dispatch, disconnect accounting, doc mirror gating, thumbnail bucketing, and the 400 ms state. None has a JVM test, because tv-app has no unit-test source set. Only the wrong-PIN refusal is asserted anywhere, by the device-bound live UI test. PLATFORM-RISK.md says the meaning moved into PenSessionHost and that core is what ports, so the meaning sits in the one module that does not port. The logic touches Android only through Log and the Thumbnailer, so moving it costs a small effects vocabulary and no new dependency: core stays kotlinx-serialization only, with no coroutines.

## Flow
- LanTransport or RelayTransport hands PenSessionHost a PenChannel (unchanged)
- Host creates `PenConversation(desk, openedAtMs)`; a watchdog coroutine calls `onTick(now)` once at the timeout
- `receiveLoop` feeds each frame to `onText`; the host carries out the effects: `Send` -> channel.send(encode), `Close` -> channel.close, `Deliver` -> session.accept, `Paired` -> penConnected, log line and heartbeat start
- The heartbeat loop builds a `HeartbeatInput` from Session, calls `beat`, fetches a thumbnail on Dispatchers.IO only if `thumbnailAtMs != null`, and sends doc then state
- `finally` stays in the host (penDisconnected)

## Expected impact
Eleven behaviours get 8 JUnit cases in `:core:test`, which runs in about 6 s with no device, instead of a ~60 s emulator run that covers one of them. PenSessionHost goes from 170 lines to roughly 70 lines of plumbing. A builder in this harness, which has no emulator, can now verify pairing and heartbeat changes. A Vega port, and the desk's reuse of the same contract, get a tested reference rather than Android code to reverse-engineer.

## Evaluation
Claim: the TV's pen protocol logic becomes JVM-tested and portable with no change to the wire.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (the classes do not exist). 0 of 11 host behaviours have a JVM test.
After: 8 of 8. `:tv-app:compileDebugKotlin` is green with the host delegating.
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: none

cards.title: Review mode: drawn moments on the scrub bar, one tap to jump to each
shared_surfaces: tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/PenSessionHost.kt (card A rewrites it; B's edit is one field on the state message, landed after A into Heartbeat's input)
acceptance: case 1 (JUnit core ReviewModeTest): a doc with a stroke at fromMs 5000, an arrow at 5200, a stroke at 12000 and a name tag at 12040 -> AnnotationTimeline(doc).moments() == [5000, 12000]. Anchors within 500 ms cluster into one moment, taking the earliest
case 2 (JUnit core): with the same doc, momentAfter(0) == 5000; momentAfter(5000) == 12000 (sitting on a moment moves to the next one); momentAfter(12000) == null
case 3 (JUnit core): momentBefore(12000) == 5000; momentBefore(20000) == 12000; momentBefore(5100) == null
case 4 (JUnit core): PenEngine gets a stroke at 5000, then Undo -> AnnotationTimeline(engine.doc).moments() == []; then Redo -> [5000]. Erased or undone ink leaves no moment behind

case 5 (JUnit core): TransportPlan.plan(cmd="jump", value=1.0, positionMs=0, durationMs=20000, playing=true, doc) -> [Pause, SeekTo(5000)]. plan("jump", 1.0, positionMs=12000, ...) -> [] (no later drawing, nothing moves). plan("jump", -1.0, positionMs=12000, ...) -> [Pause, SeekTo(5000)]

GUARD: case 6 (JUnit core): the arithmetic MainActivity.kt:180-198 performs today moves unchanged. plan("step", 1.0, positionMs=5000) -> [Pause, SeekTo(5040)]; plan("seek-", 0.0, positionMs=3000) -> [SeekTo(0)]; plan("rate", 3.0) -> [SetRate(2.0)]; plan("toggle", 0.0, playing=true) -> [Pause]; plan("undo") -> [Edit(PenMessage.Undo)]

case 7 (JUnit core): TvMessage.State(t=0, paused=true, rate=1.0, annotationCount=2, marks=listOf(5000, 12000)).encode() contains "marks":[5000,12000]. Decoding '{"type":"state","t":1,"paused":true,"rate":1.0,"annotationCount":0}' with ProtocolJson gives marks == [] (older senders still decode)

tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt:124-133 - the remote seeks in blind 5 s hops (seek+/seek-, applied at :183-184), and the phone has frame step and scrub, so returning to a drawn frame means scrubbing and watching the TV
MainActivity.kt:177-203 - the whole transport interpretation (toggle, step x FRAME_MS=40 (:51), rate clamp 0.1..2.0, seek clamp at 0) lives inside a Composable LaunchedEffect with no test

core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenEngine.kt:13-19 (Hold) - ink is anchored to its frame and expires after 3/6/15 s, so a review of several moments is exactly the case where the drawings are off screen and have to be found again
tools/live-ui-test.mjs:125-136 and :175-191 - even the harness finds its drawing again by counting D-pad hops from a known position, which is the viewer's problem in miniature

Protocol.kt:125-130 - ProtocolJson has ignoreUnknownKeys=true, encodeDefaults=true and explicitNulls=false, so an added list field with a default of emptyList() is backward compatible for Kotlin readers. JS readers ignore unknown fields

Consumers of TvMessage.State (the contract change): companion/index.html:170-201 applyState; tools/relay-stub.mjs:91-96 spreads state into /health (it gains marks, which is harmless); tools/relay-test.mjs:200-234 and tools/pen-sim.mjs:44-47 read other fields; tools/live-ui-test.mjs:429 via window.__pen.state; core ProtocolTest (CoreTest.kt:165-170, still green: an empty list encodes as [] and not null)
cards.rollback: Four commits: (1) core moments, TransportPlan and the State.marks field with tests, additive since State's default is an empty list; (2) MainActivity delegates to TransportPlan and handles jump, and Session/host publish marks; (3) companion ticks and buttons; (4) the live-ui-test journey and a README line. Reverting (3) leaves a TV that sends an unused field. Reverting (1)-(2) restores the old when-block verbatim.
cards.runner_up: A pairing card that gets out of the picture. The white QR card is always drawn over the top-right of the video (MainActivity.kt:223-228, 245-269; the harness even masks it out at live-ui-test.mjs:56). It would collapse to a chip once a pen is connected and come back, with the reason, when the pen drops or a wrong PIN is tried.
cards.body:
## Summary
Give the telestrator a review mode. The TV publishes the list of drawn moments, the phone's scrub bar shows them as ticks, and two buttons (previous drawing / next drawing) send a new transport command `jump`. The TV answers `jump` by pausing on the exact frame the ink is anchored to. The decision about which moment comes next is made in core (`AnnotationTimeline.moments/momentAfter/momentBefore`), next to a `TransportPlan` that pulls the untested transport when-block out of a Composable.

## Description
A telestrator is used to draw on several paused frames and then walk someone through them. Today the walk-through is blind. Ink expires after its hold window, the phone forgets the mirrored doc once playback starts, the scrub bar is an unmarked range, and the remote seeks in 5 s hops. To find drawing number three, the viewer scrubs and watches the TV until ink appears, even though the TV holds a `fromMs` for every annotation. The data is already there, and this card puts it where the navigation decision is made. The move also turns the transport interpretation into a pure function (`plan(cmd, value, positionMs, durationMs, playing, doc) -> List<PlayerAction>`), so frame step, the rate clamp and the new jump are tested on the JVM rather than only on a device. This is inside the companion's declared scope ('transport'), but the tv-app and companion map descriptions do not name drawn-moment navigation, hence gate direction. It is also a contract change, an added optional `marks: List<Long>` on `TvMessage.State`; every consumer is listed in the premise and none breaks.

## Flow
- Viewer draws on frames at 5.0 s and 12.0 s (as today)
- Each 400 ms state now carries `marks: [5000, 12000]` (from Session -> engine.doc -> AnnotationTimeline.moments)
- Phone: the scrub bar shows two ticks at marks/duration; the status reads 'drawing 1 of 2' when t sits on a mark; [prev drawing] / [next drawing] are disabled at the ends
- Tap [next drawing] -> `{type:'transport', cmd:'jump', value:1}` -> TV `TransportPlan.plan` -> Pause + SeekTo(12000) -> the frame and its ink are on screen, and the thumbnail and mirror follow through the existing paused heartbeat
- The remote is unchanged (D-pad and FF/RW keep their meanings); binding FF/RW to jump while paused is left for later

## Expected impact
Returning to any drawn frame takes one tap instead of an open-ended scrub-and-look loop, and the ticks show where every drawing is before the viewer moves at all. Presenting a play review becomes a sequence of next taps. The transport rules get their first tests: 5 transport verbs pinned by a GUARD case.

## Evaluation
Claim: the viewer can reach every drawn moment directly, and the transport decisions become JVM-tested.
Before: 0 of 7 JVM acceptance cases pass (moments, TransportPlan and marks do not exist). Returning to a drawing takes an unbounded number of scrub steps.
After: 7 of 7 in `:core:test`, `:tv-app:compileDebugKotlin` green. Case 8 is an operator-run device journey.
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: direction
cards.evidence: Timeline.kt (whole class, 17 lines): only `visibleAt(tMs)` and `progressAt(a, tMs)`; no enumeration of moments. Protocol.kt:95-106 `data class State(val t: Long, val paused: Boolean, val rate: Double, val annotationCount: Int, val canUndo: Boolean = false, val canRedo: Boolean = false, val durationMs: Long = 0, val thumbnail: String? = null)`. companion/index.html:117-120 `0.0s`, with no marks. companion/index.html:195-198 `} else if (!m.paused) { pad.style.backgroundImage = ''; tvDoc = null; ...}`. MainActivity.kt:128-129 `KEYCODE_MEDIA_FAST_FORWARD, KEYCODE_DPAD_RIGHT -> "seek+"` / `REWIND, DPAD_LEFT -> "seek-"`; :183-184 `seekTo(currentPosition +/- 5_000)`. MainActivity.kt:188-192 `"step" -> { player.pause(); val target = player.currentPosition + (t.value.toLong() * FRAME_MS); player.seekTo(target.coerceAtLeast(0)) }` sits inside `LaunchedEffect(command)` (:177), and no test covers it. Protocol.kt:125-130 `ProtocolJson = Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true; encodeDefaults = true; classDiscriminator = "type"; explicitNulls = false }`. relay-stub.mjs:93-96 `if (m.type === 'state') { const { thumbnail, ...rest } = m; lastState = rest; }`, so the new field passes through to /health untouched.

critic.deck_line: Approve (direction): the viewer reaches any drawn frame in one tap instead of scrubbing and watching; the transport rules get their first tests.
